incidents.victim: ConnectWise (hundreds of Cloud Backup / Microsoft 365 customer tenants)
incidents.vector: China-aligned actor Storm-0940 used the agentic-AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX to steal a sensitive API secret and abuse already-authorized ConnectWise Cloud Backup application access into customer Microsoft 365 tenants.
incidents.impact: Nearly 1,000 Entra tenants saw sign-in attempts and over 300 succeeded; ConnectWise suspended Cloud Backup, SaaS Security and Cloud Management services for days while customers reviewed Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint and Graph API activity for compromise.

incidents.victim: 20+ Japanese companies and South Korean banks
incidents.vector: An unidentified actor used the same Artex agentic-AI attack tool seen in the ConnectWise campaign to automate intrusions against Japanese firms and, separately, South Korean banks and financial institutions.
incidents.impact: Japanese security firm GMO confirmed at least 20 Japanese companies were breached; it did not confirm whether the same actor was behind the earlier South Korean bank attacks.

incidents.victim: 600+ organizations across critical infrastructure sectors in the Americas, Europe, and Australia
incidents.vector: SafePay actors compromise credentials and exploit known vulnerabilities in internet-facing and VPN devices, then use legitimate IT tools to move laterally and disable backups before exfiltrating data and encrypting systems.
incidents.impact: CISA, FBI, Secret Service and international partners jointly warned that SafePay is one of the most active ransomware groups of 2026, with victims pressured via data-leak threats and direct calls demanding payment.

incidents.victim: Hundreds of PHP-based websites and services worldwide
incidents.vector: Two critical PHP core vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, dubbed 'PHP2Shell', CVSS 9.2) allow unauthenticated remote code execution in code paths touched by nearly every PHP request.
incidents.impact: Cloudflare and watchTowr observed in-the-wild exploitation attempts, including AI-generated proof-of-concept tools, and hundreds of sites went offline as administrators scrambled to patch after the PHP Foundation's emergency release.

incidents.victim: Global TLS and code-signing trust infrastructure (eMudhra-issued certificates)
incidents.vector: A 2025 key-generation flaw at certificate authority eMudhra produced eight intermediate CA private keys with only 3-8 bits of effective entropy instead of 384, making the keys trivially recoverable and allowing forged, trusted certificates for any website or code-signing target.
incidents.impact: Chrome, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft blocked the affected certificates and Mozilla removed eMudhra's root from Firefox; Go also shipped a patched release to reject the compromised certificate chains across container and cloud-native tooling.

incidents.victim: Tor network (330+ relays, over 10% of exit nodes)
incidents.vector: An attacker hacked Tor relay servers, infected them with the Ebury Linux malware, and converted them into malicious exit relays to intercept SSH sessions and downgrade and steal unencrypted email traffic.
incidents.impact: The mass-sniffing campaign spread to more than 10% of Tor exit relays before a Swiss engineer detected it; the Tor Project blocklisted and removed the compromised servers from the network.

incidents.victim: At least two Indian universities
incidents.vector: An actor operating under the handle BUGSTER configured the Hermes Agent framework with DeepSeek V4 and a jailbroken AI assistant to run brute-force and intrusion campaigns, also building pipelines for VoIP fraud, Wi-Fi password cracking and cryptocurrency-whale reconnaissance.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed a successful intrusion at one university with exfiltration of more than 5,200 student records containing personally identifiable information, plus a brute-force campaign against a second university's website.

incidents.victim: A NATO-member naval shipbuilder, a military aircraft-engine maker, and a law enforcement agency
incidents.vector: GRU-linked hackers used a previously undocumented loader and the Hookedge backdoor to gain footholds, with hands-on-keyboard operators returning repeatedly over a week to steal credentialed material.
incidents.impact: Symantec confirmed credential theft from a compromised host at the shipbuilder and identified the law enforcement agency and aircraft-engine maker as additional espionage targets, part of a broader campaign against European defense and diplomatic targets.

incidents.victim: John Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins, and 100+ other e-commerce and payment-processing sites
incidents.vector: A Chinese-speaking actor used the AI-driven penetration-testing tool Cairn, run through publicly exposed dashboards, to automate vulnerability discovery (SQLi, insecure deserialization, auth bypass) and deploy web shells across targets, costing roughly $5,000 in AI tokens.
incidents.impact: Researchers at NorForge found over 1,100 automated attack projects across 14 exposed dashboards; John Deere and SharkNinja said incidents were contained with no confirmed sensitive-data access, while Cummins was investigating a third-party vendor site compromise.

incidents.victim: California public school students (via contractor Educational Testing Service)
incidents.vector: A months-long cyberattack compromised systems at Educational Testing Service, a testing contractor for California's Department of Education, exposing data collected through statewide assessment programs.
incidents.impact: Stolen data covers current and former students enrolled since 2006, including names, birthdates, addresses, SSIDs, disability status, English-learner status and federal program eligibility for more than 5.7 million students.

incidents.victim: Alternative for Germany (AfD) political party
incidents.vector: A hacker breached AfD's web hosting provider and obtained internal email inboxes, website databases and private documents.
incidents.impact: 281GB of leaked data was published, exposing internal party communications; the party claimed the email accounts were long-abandoned, though some leaked threads dated to this year.

incidents.victim: Staples
incidents.vector: A Chinese organized crime group gained access to Staples' internal gift-card management application, known as Nexus.
incidents.impact: The group issued more than 15,000 fraudulent gift cards worth over $5 million for retailers including Target and Sephora, using them to buy goods shipped to China for resale.

incidents.victim: H2O Retailing / Hankyu Hanshin department stores
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a website operated by Hankyu Hanshin, one of H2O Retailing's department store brands.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to 1.26 million customers was stolen in the breach.

incidents.victim: Nikkei
incidents.vector: Hackers used stolen credentials to access a Nikkei cloud server, the company's third breach in the past month.
incidents.impact: 1.83 million records were stolen from the compromised cloud server.

incidents.victim: Qubic (cryptocurrency platform) users
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited insufficiently random wallet seed-phrase generation affecting iOS and macOS users to steal from Qubic customer accounts.
incidents.impact: Roughly $1.4 million was stolen; Qubic halted operations and froze about 87% of the stolen funds while working to restore them to affected customers.

incidents.victim: National Radiocommunications Company (Radiocom), Romania
incidents.vector: A cyberattack crippled the internal IT network of Romania's state-owned radio and TV signal broadcaster.
incidents.impact: Radiocom shut down its email server to contain the attack; the company said its radio communications broadcast network itself was not affected.

incidents.victim: Ukraine state data-exchange platform
incidents.vector: A Russian-speaking threat actor gained access to an exposed Elasticsearch server belonging to Ukraine's state data-exchange platform.
incidents.impact: 6.8 million documents were stolen from the government platform.

incidents.victim: Zeabur (AI DevOps platform) customers
incidents.vector: A hacker breached Zeabur's systems and stole environment variables and other sensitive records; the platform was also breached in August via its AWS backend.
incidents.impact: More than 320,000 accounts had data exposed in this, the platform's second breach of the year; Zeabur announced it will shut down entirely at the end of 2026.

incidents.victim: OVHcloud CLI tool users
incidents.vector: An attacker compromised a developer's GitHub account and published malicious versions (v0.11.0-v0.15.0) of OVHcloud's command-line tool containing a binary designed to harvest local secrets.
incidents.impact: The tampered package was live for under two hours before OVHcloud detected and blocked it; affected users were urged to update to the clean v0.16.0 release and rotate all local secrets.

incidents.victim: LOXONE
incidents.vector: Hackers breached the German smart-home and building-automation vendor's internal IT network over a weekend.
incidents.impact: LOXONE shut down its internal IT network to contain the intrusion; the company said the incident did not spread to customer systems, which run on localized mini-servers.

incidents.victim: TeamUpdraft (WordPress plugin developer) and downstream customer sites
incidents.vector: Attackers accessed TeamUpdraft's backend database over a weekend, stealing customer account data and site connection keys, then used those keys to connect directly to customer WordPress sites.
incidents.impact: Security firm Wordfence found the stolen keys were used to deploy malicious plugins onto affected customer sites.
